conflict.question: Whether the target moved or closed, is a stale wrong-location target, or remains identity-ambiguous; and whether it may be verified with all frozen rows excluded as location_mismatch.

Earlier node history shows the same coordinates under Bombay Indian, so the OSM name and website fields are historical point-in-time tags, not proof that the Silver Spring target moved to Germantown.

The current restaurant-controlled site identifies Curry Place Silver Spring at exactly 11229 New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD 20904, with phone 301-593-7222, current daily hours, dine-in, takeout, delivery, menu, and ordering links. The address and phone exactly match the target node.

The site used by Luna identifies Curry Place Germantown at 12951 Wisteria Dr, Germantown, MD 20874, phone 301-972-1005. Its different address and phone distinguish it from the simultaneously represented Silver Spring restaurant.
The frozen Luna evidence establishes only the Germantown identity of curryplacemd.com; it does not establish closure, relocation, or nonexistence of the Silver Spring target.

Because Luna inspected the distinct Germantown site and reconciled all 177 frozen rows solely on that mistaken scope, its menu boundary and reconciliation cannot satisfy terminal verification for Silver Spring.
